title: FrontierOR: Benchmarking LLMs' Capacity for Efficient Algorithm Design in Large-Scale Optimization
claim: A benchmark spans diverse problem types and realistic large scales, built through a literature-sourced, expert-audited multi-stage construction process.
layout: 2 sections: left grid of donut and histogram panels, right construction flow
description: The figure has two sections under shaded title bars. The left section, "FrontierOR Benchmark", is a grid of seven labeled panels. Panels a–d are donut charts with percentage slices for problem class, formulation type, decision horizon and application field. Panels e–g are stacked histograms of Gurobi solve time, variable count and constraint count, with the hard set in orange and other tasks in purple. The right section, "Benchmark Construction", has two dashed boxes. The first, "I Source Selection", shows a fan of journal-paper thumbnails and three bullets, including 180 papers. The second, "II Task Formulation", is a flowchart. Information Extraction and Component Generation boxes feed a stack of outputs, including problem description, formulation, instances, Gurobi program and feasibility checker. These are followed by a checklist, Expert Audit, and an Accept/Reject Agent Repair loop. The eye goes first to the colorful donuts on the left.

In panels (e), (f), and (g), the vertical axis Count denotes the number of FrontierOR tasks. Those optimization tasks contain up to 108 variables and over 107 constraints. 48.1% of the large-instance reference runs exceed the one-hour runtime budget. We construct the benchmark by collecting problems from leading OR journals, and ensure data quality through multi-round expert review.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for optimization modeling and solver-code generation, yet practical operations research and optimization problems often require a harder capability: designing scalable algorithms that exploit problem structure and outperform direct formulation-and-solve baselines. Existing benchmarks are limited to small or simplified examples far below real-world scale and complexity. We introduce FrontierOR, the first literature-grounded benchmark targeting LLM-generated algorithm efficiency on realistic large-scale optimization problems. FrontierOR includes 180 diverse tasks, each derived from a paper published in a top-tier operations research venue, with standardized instances and a hidden, expert-verified evaluation suite. We evaluate recent LLMs' one-shot algorithm generation and improvements achieved through several self-evolving frameworks. The results show that current models still struggle to move from executable formulations to efficient optimization algorithms. Even the strongest LLM succeeds on only 39% of Full-set task instances, where success is defined as returning a feasible solution with an objective gap of at most 1% relative to Gurobi within its runtime. On the Hard subset, test-time evolution raises this proportion from 51% for the strongest one-shot model to 78%. FrontierOR provides a continuously maintained testbed for evaluating LLM-designed optimization algorithms under a shared protocol and controlled computational settings. Code and data are publicly released at https://github.com/Minw913/FrontierOR.
